newsitem.title: USA: AOL says technical glitch caused errors in quotes.
newsitem.headline: AOL says technical glitch caused errors in quotes.

text.p: A technical "glitch" caused America Online Inc to display incorrect stock prices and trading volumes on some over-the-counter stocks earlier this week, a spokeswoman said.
America Online said it noticed the problem on Tuesday, March 4 and corrected the situation on Wednesday.

America Online said "faulty data" was provided by Standard & Poors due to a transmission error. This technical problem caused America Online to display incorrect stock quotes and trading volume activity on some small capitalization stocks, said Tricia Primrose, a spokeswoman for America Online.
Dulles, Va-based America Online said it does not know how many over-the-counter stocks were effected by the errors.
Officials from Standard & Poors, owned by McGraw-Hill Cos Inc, did not return calls seeking comment.
Ben Ezra Weinstein and Co said it was one of the victims of the error. Ben Ezra said the errors displayed on America Online caused "great confusion in the marketplace."
Ben Ezra develops Internet-compatible programs to help companies in the procedure of filing public or private offerings.
